label: Choice-cell determination laws, from the definitions
description: A placed diagnostic for 608a262d. An invariant explanans (the kind an existential PSR reason token can be) explains the realized range of outcomes and no contrast within it (law 3); selecting a contingent outcome requires an explanans level whose own cell is contingent and is not seen to by any invariant level (law 6). The value of laws 7 and 8 is negative: determination on cells reads only cell partitions, and any level as fine as the outcome partition, including a bare re-description of the outcome, meets it. So this standard cannot discriminate explaining the selection from re-describing it, nor an adoption from an actualization. A discriminating test needs a standard on which the explanans is individuated independently of the outcome partition, or a different sense of selecting (SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_1, pro tanto favouring), neither tested here. Establishes no premise.
